sections.html: The emperor tetra (Nematobrycon palmeri) has for decades been one of the most beloved tetra species of all, thanks to its great beauty and interesting behaviour.

The species is available all year round as captive-bred fish. Wild-collected fish, on the other hand, are available only seasonally. Wild-collected and captive-bred emperor tetras differ, as in most tetra species, mainly in body shape: wild fish are much more slender than captive-bred ones, because food in the wild is far less abundant than it usually is in aquaria. In coloration there is no difference between wild and captive-bred fish: both are very beautiful.
